text: The award step builds against the plan's H row and treats the rwb-case state and move, the rwb-decision package and approval chain, the rwb-access DoA limit and the rwb-source-data score as class C rows it declares and fakes in the text, without adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the case state and move, the rule package, the DoA limit, the approval chain and the model score, and three of those operations have no published name.
read: The six consumed rows are named in 12.2 with their owners and placeholders, faked in 12.8 and named in the dependency text of section 13; the case move is read as the workflow stage outcome; no C row is added to the metadata table.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-source-data
impact: The story can start on Day 1 against fakes; the dependency map under-reports six rows and one Temporal queue dependency until it is corrected

text: The award publishes rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1 (EV-23) from the outbox in the same transaction as the lot update, and DP-09 with RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as an absent library row rather than added to the H row.
why: TSD S6 T5.3 publishes LotAwarded and the slide 13 matrix shows rwb-payment and rwb-reporting listening to the service, while the plan's pattern set carries DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only and the H row has no outbox library story.
read: The event, its topic, its CloudEvents envelope, its payload and its two consumers are declared in 12.3 and in the CON; outbox_event sits in the schema as a library object; no event is consumed at this step.
applied_in: Metadata (Patterns applied, Depends on (build)); Sections 4, 8, 12.3, 12.7 and 13
confirm: Platform library owner and the owners of rwb-payment and rwb-reporting
impact: The event is built once per award with the library that the plan does not list, and the consumer contracts are unblocked

text: The FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and the TSD S6 Debt sale v2 module files stand in for the absent S6 extract and are the source text of this step.
why: The run's extract folder holds no S6 module file, and the module documents sit above any summary in the precedence order of R7.3.
read: Every value of sections 2 to 18 is taken from the legacy story, the FSD S6 v3, the TSD S6 v2, the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 or the context pack, and section 18 names the two module files as the source text.
impact: No value is taken from a summary or a deck; the extract set is one module pair short until it is rebuilt

text: The story keeps the EP06 wave 4 and the 30 April 2027 release, marked tentative, while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3.
why: R5.6 keeps the later W-MAP wave, the WP and the legacy epic give wave 4 and 30 April 2027, and U7 forbids moving or raising a date.
read: The plan's wave and release values are copied unchanged, the release is marked tentative in the metadata and in section 2, and the wave difference is recorded once for S6 and EP06
impact: Sequencing is unchanged and one service delivers in two waves with two releases

text: The four legacy criteria are kept word for word; this story builds the price test, the award route and the winning buyer, names R-DS-04's effect with RWB-S6-E5024-APP and RWB-S6-E6001-APP, and names R-DS-23, the agreement and the move to LOT_AWARDED with RWB-S6-E6006-APP.
why: The legacy key owns four criteria that touch three sibling steps, the target split gives each step its own story, and the FSD and the TSD map REQ-S6-006 differently.
read: The four scenarios keep the legacy lines unchanged and add only the contract-mock Given lines; R-DS-04 and R-DS-23 are tabled in section 8; section 19 names the sibling stories; REQ-S6-006 is traced with the TSD mapping difference recorded
confirm: Business analyst and the owners of RWB-S6-E5024-APP, RWB-S6-E6001-APP and RWB-S6-E6006-APP
impact: No criterion is silently reworded and no sibling field is claimed; the criterion-to-story boundary is explicit for the wave 4 harness

text: The best bid, its time and the price achieved are carried in the decision record and the operation contracts because no bid or award-price column exists; the award writes only buyer_partner_id and buyer_class, reads the score on the rwb-source-data contract, and reads the cap and the reserve rule with their version.
why: R-DS-19 compares the best bid to the reserve and the cap and API-S6-003 awards the lot, while TSD S6 T3.1 has no bid table and no bid or award-price column, no source states the buyer-class rule, the legacy v_ace_score view is P1's alone, and no source gives the score field IDs.
read: Section 11 declares the bid and award price as Not specified in the source documents, the lot writes are limited to DF-SAL-025 and DF-SAL-026, the score is a consumed row with its as-of date and model version, and the values stay in the package and reference data
confirm: Data steward, the solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner
impact: The award is buildable and testable on the fakes; the price evidence lives in the decision record until a column set is agreed, and no ACE grant is requested
